name: Sparkle Caddis Pupa
imitates: Gary LaFontaine's emergent caddis pupa; the Antron shuck traps air bubbles like the gas sheath on a real hatching pupa. Fish it in the film or as a dropper behind a dry during a caddis hatch.

steps.text: Start the thread two eye lengths behind the eye, wrap a thread base to the bend and return to the starting point.
Tie in a third of a strand of tan sparkle yarn at the starting point.
Pull the yarn around the shank toward the bend, wrap back over it to the bend, then return the thread to mid-shank.
Dub a reverse-tapered abdomen, thin at the front and fuller toward the rear, ending at the bend.
Wrap the thread forward over the dubbed abdomen in open spirals to the front.
Press the yarn forward from the bend so it encircles the body.
Pull the yarn tightly forward past the hook eye.
Push it back again to leave some slack over the body, forming a loose shroud.
Tie the yarn off at the front of the abdomen.
Pick out a little yarn on top with scissor tips and cut it near the front so it trails back as the shuck. Clip the excess yarn and build a thread base over the butts.
Peel a few fibers from a black marabou feather.
Tie the marabou fibers in by their tips at the front of the body and clip the tips.
Wrap the marabou forward to the eye, tie off, clip the excess, build a smooth thread head and whip finish.
